notes.title: Versebound Patch 1.0.2
notes.content:
[h1]Moikka![/h1]

Versebound has been out for a month now, and we've gotten lots of feedback, which has been great! Many of you have also given us ideas for improvements in terms of quality of life options and balance. We managed to implement most of the requested things in this patch, along with some bug fixes. Controller support was also on the list, and we tried our best to implement it, but in the end it proved too difficult with the current logic in the game. We did learn many things by digging in to the possibilities on that front, so for our future games we'll for sure manage it easily as we'll be able to design it in properly from the start. :)

But anyway, here are the patch notes!

[h3]Balance:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Reduced Tapio’s HP
[*] Reduced the amount of Trial of Mielikki mushrooms in Tuonela
[*] Reduced the XP multiplier of Luonto
[*] Ukko's Wedge rotation speed fade out time prolonged
[*] Etiäinen taunting shadow lifetime up
[*] Triggering Snowshoes of kauppi is now easier
[*] Shortened Aino Skill end animation duration -> now resuming movement is faster
[*] Reduced Aino Skill cooldowns across all levels
[*] Poem of Henki now also heals for 2HP upon updating max health
[*] Increased Poem of Henki weapon damage +%
[*] Poem of Hurme HP per kill per level increased
[*] Increased Poem of Vaski dmg reduction %
[*] Harpoon knockback down across all levels
[*] Harpoon damage up across all levels (except imbued)
[*] Bear Trap lv 1-5 damage down
[*] Bear Trap lv 1-5 cooldowns up slightly
[*] Vengeful Tears trail lifespan slightly up
[*] Spirit of Kaleva base damage up
[*] Spirit of Kaleva damage increase upon player hit down
[*] Pike Jawbone damage up across all levels
[*] Northern Breeze lv 4-5 & imbued knockback down
[*] Northern Breeze lv 1-5 rotation speed down
[*] Northern Breeze damage up across all levels
[/list]

[h3]Quality of life settings:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added an option to aim the Skill to movement direction
[*] Added an option to toggle a visible attack direction indicator
[*] Added an option to toggle enemy hit indicators
[*] Added an option to reroll upgrades once per level
[/list]

[h3]Bug fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Arrow to stone altar now correctly disappears if no Väki is left after opening the door in Tuonela unlock
[*] Fixed a bug where pause menu could be opened before the scene has faded
[*] Fixed a bug where picking up a Tuonela ritual flower exactly when the ritual is failed resets the timer and bugs out the ritual
[*] Maybe fixed a bug where player might get stuck in the level borders
[*] Maybe fixed a bug where harpoon might stop attacking upon reaching near 0% cooldown
[*] Maybe fixed a bug where Tuonela's river might stop damaging player after Cloudberry invulnerability effect ends
[/list]

[h3]Other:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Reworded Ilmarinen’s first task to be more clear
[*] Reframed some text info in settings menu to be more clear
[*] Tuonela unlock should now be less confusing
[*] Whitecurrants now drop with a higher chance
[*] Invulnerability duration can now be prolonged upon eating another Cloudberry when invulnerability is active
[/list]

notes.title: Plans for the near future
notes.content:
[h1]Hello there![/h1]

Thank you for all the feedback and reviews you have given us! We appreciate it a lot!
It has been very exciting for us to see you play Versebound :)

[h2]Suomi Survivors Bundle[/h2]
We have bundled up with another Finnish developer Antti Vaihia to bring you the ultimate Finnish survivors experience! 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2178560/Horde_Hunters/

[b]Horde Hunters[/b] is a very in-depth take on the survivors genre with a lot of stats and synergies as well as tons of stuff to do! You can get both games now with a 10% discount!

[h2]What's next?[/h2]
We have gathered all the feedback and wishes from all the platforms (Discord & Steam). Keep them coming, we are constantly reading everything and nothing is left out of consideration.

We will start making changes based on their importance as well as how efficiently we can implement them. Currently on the list are the following:
[list]
[*] Balance tweaks
[*] QOL-options
[*] Reworking some stuff that are confusing
[/list]
We are also aware that there are multiple requests for [b]controller support[/b]. We are looking into it! At this time we can't make promises, but your wishes have been heard :)

Thanks for your feedback and support for Versebound, it's been awesome!

Until we meet again.

notes.title: Progress news!
notes.content:
[h1]Hello to all of you kind people![/h1]

We are working hard on finishing the rest of the content needed for the release that is coming fairly soon (yay!). We are making good progress, but there still remains a lot to do! Here's a brief take on what's been happening: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/af968e26aca99e0a6cbe6995a1d2e96c62da64f1.png[/img]

[h2]First of all, thank you for the feedback![/h2]
We have received a lot of feedback, bug reports and ideas from you! Some content creators have also taken the time to make videos about Versebound. Thank you for that. Obviously we can't make every wish come true, but you are helping us improve the game. 

For example, [b]we heard that you don't like the bow.[/b] We get it. That's why it has received an update on it's logic (available in the full release). There are also some aspects about the game that may not be clear for the player. We will improve that too. Also all the bug reports are being monitored and fixed. 

So thank you for taking the time to try Versebound, and keep the feedback coming! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/e731b7a9bfe34b0acaed4c6885d062b665f1588f.png[/img]

[h2]We are making progress:[/h2]

We are happy to tell you, that all the [b]rituals, weapons and trials are DONE[/b] with the exception of some graphics and SFX's! 

[b]The hub[/b] has also received an update to it's layout. It's even more cozy now :)

Most of our time at the moment is going to finishing the second map! This means new enemy designs, the boss fight, secrets etc. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/4912bf35def673ee75eada80413b9dbb1b42d03c.png[/img]

[h2]The demo will be up for another week[/h2] 
and after that, we will remove it from Steam as we go into the last month before full release (at the end of April). So now you still have a good amount of time to finish the demo if you haven't already. 

Thanks for your interest for Versebound, we will get back to you shortly!

notes.title: Forward! Said grandma in the snow.
notes.content:
[h1]A lot has happened in the last couple of weeks.[/h1]
We released a demo, did a stream, participated in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/nextfest]Steam Next Fest[/url] which is soon over and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45022621/sale/RamadanFestival2025]The Days of the Ramadan[/url] festival started! During these times, we haven't been resting and taking it easy. No! We have been hard at work listening to your feedback, fixing bugs and optimizing the game. We also released a whole new mechanic to the game on our latest patch update. Read more about it [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2672520/view/528713272771218218?l=english]here[/url]. 

Now it's time for us to turn our heads forward towards the full release! We are already well on our way to finishing the second map as well as all the other new content. But there's still a lot to do. The next month or so we will focus heavily on finishing the game! 

Even though we will be focusing on new content and the Steam Next Fest is ending, the current demo will still be playable for some time. 

[h1]Updates & Progress[/h1]
[h2]Made the third and final character for Versebound: Aino! The team is now complete![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/c30cca6a057d7310f5e378e219f8c908a901be3d.png[/img]
She is fast and can teleport for a short distance! Her playstyle revolves quite a lot around her movement skill and experience gain. Her damage output is not that strong though, so getting through the difficult early game is the key to victory

[h2]Added a feature many testers have hoped for: the ability to use Skills in Hub![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/6585d7552da65224c160faf80cde15d828eb6f7a.gif[/img]
Skills are character specific movement abilities that bring dynamic vibes to the gameplay! It was a bit of a hassle as the Hub wasn’t designed for Skills and Skills weren’t designed to be used in the Hub. But as always, I made it work!

[h2]Added kill amounts to bestiary entries![/h2]
Now there is something to do for those who like to see big numbers! Can you get a million Kyy (snake) kills?

[h2]Did the final secret boss of our game![/h2]
This one is a classic dual boss, where the player is tested with a melee and a ranged boss at once! Once managing to fell one of them, the remaining one goes into a rage mode and challenges the player’s skills with advanced attacks to avenge their companion! That’s going to be causing some panic in the release for sure.. Also, now there is only one more boss to make, wonder who that could be..?

[h2]Other updates[/h2]
[list]
[*] Did a weapon unlock quest chain for the first unlockable weapon of Tuonela! It involves mysterious wintery statues, freezing gusts of air in a snow-covered forest, and bottles. Yep, definitely Finland.
[*] Did lots of bug fixes and small tweaks! These are good to do in a batch once in a while, and give nice variation to the usual grind 🙂
[*] Added logic for unique “player damaged” sound effects. Now it’s needed since our cast of characters also has a female in it.
[*] Added Aino unlock event to our second map, Tuonela! Now almost everything regarding playable characters is done! Woop woop!
[*] Did LOTS of tweaking, bug fixing and polishing for our final public demo! It’s been quite crazy, but I managed to do everything that was planned and even some “nice to have” things, like the[b] long-awaited hover menu system[/b] that let’s players check precise stats of their equipment. It was a total hassle and I almost went a bit crazy trying to make it work, but managed in the end, and now it works perfectly!
[*] Did lots of scene tweaks and made great progress on the second map of Versebound, Tuonela! Also implemented one cool visual gimmick for one of their bosses, it’s quite nasty now!
[*] Updated main menu graphics
[*] New SFX for XP Fairy artifact
[*] Updated graphics for Poem of Oppi
[*] New SFX’s for when Joukahainen gets freed
[*] [b]We’ve gotten lots of amazing feedback[/b] from the demo testers, super hyped about that! However, we’ve also gotten reports of heavy, yet seemingly random fps drops during runs. While we had no clear idea what might cause this, there was one huge thing that could be regarding optimization: enemy pooling. Most of the often used objects are already recycled in Versebound, but I had made the base for the enemyspawner two years ago, and then I was just too lazy to implement pooling there. Also I didn’t have the skills to do that properly. Now I have though, so it seemed like the correct moment to implement that!
[/list]

Expect lots of new cool content coming in the coming weeks. Until then, don't let the Hiisi eat you :)

notes.title: Kalevala day & The Days of the Ramadan
notes.content:
First of all,
[h1]Happy Kalevala day everyone![/h1]

Today is officially the day of finnish culture here in Finland, named after the epic that jumpstarted a good bit of people's interest into it a few centuries back. Coincidentally, said epic is also what most of Versebound is based on!

While Versebound started out with a different scope in mind (originally planned to be a mobile game!), two things were set from the start; we wanted to see how we could iterate and evolve the "survivors" genre with our own little ideas, and I wanted a good excuse to finally educate myself and read this imposing national classic.

End result, I feel we've definitely got a unique and attention-demanding take on the genre near completion here! I haven't seen quite this mix of elements in any other game yet. As for my education, what I found in Kalevala was both compelling stories told in a unique poetry metre, and an inspiring fantasy setting fit to go against the modern greats! I have a feeling the influence of Kalevala will show in all my future fantasy work to come.

-Jyri, Conifer's resident lorebeard

[b]In addition to celebrating Kalevala Day, we’re also taking part in:[/b]

[h1]The Days of Ramadan – a festival celebrating Ramadan![/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/afc482b1abdacdc7da2a96807473b3b991374356.png[/img]

Check out all the amazing games featured in this event here:
https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45022621/sale/RamadanFestival2025

Let’s all enjoy a peaceful Kalevala Day and a peaceful month of Ramadan—while playing Versebound, of course.

See you soon!

notes.title: Demo update & Steam Next Fest
notes.content:
[h1]We are taking part in the Steam Next Fest that started TODAY![/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/e0e557bc56fe067e61ae332ec0219c76839c06b7.png[/img]
Go check out some of those sweet demos and upcoming games and see if you can spot [b]Versebound[/b] in there ;) And if you haven't already, now is the perfect time to [b]test out our demo[/b], since we have a treat for you:

[h1]We are introducing a completely new way of progression to Versebound! [/h1]
It's something a bit crazy, something our community didn't expect, but also something that has been requested a lot! [b]We are bringing stat based meta progression to the world of Kalevala![/b] We've been really happy with the balance of the game, and it has served our hardcore audience well. On the other hand, most of the new players we've gotten feedback from have mentioned the game being too hard. And everyone who has ever balanced anything knows that it's always a subjective matter, it's always unbalanced to someone. 
The core idea of Versebound is, and has always been, to progress through skill and knowledge, by learning through every defeat and getting a bit farther every time. And we don't want to stray from that path. So, we came up with our own way to add stat based meta progression into the mix. Something that still keeps the game challenging to the hardcore audience, but also makes it more approachable for the players who enjoy grinding for stats as well! It's our way of doing it, and we are pretty psyched about it! We haven't yet had actual unbiased testers try it out though, so let's see how everyone likes it! We are not going to explain it further than that, play the game and find out how it works! 😊

On other news, [b]there's now also environmental sounds in the Hub! [/b]Audio is an amazing way to bring the gaming experience alive, and we for sure want our game to feel immersive! We are keen to hear your feedback about this new addition as well.

On other other news, we've also made some minor tweaks to the game, like small bug and text fixes, and added some UI juice too!

The bug that causes some seemingly random, yet dramatic lag spikes is being inspected, hopefully we'll find the solution to that soon as well!

Have fun with the new update and let us know what you think :)

notes.title: Myths & Legends Sale & The Lore Behind Versebound!
notes.content:
[h1]Terve! [/h1]
[h2]It's Jyri, Conifer's resident lorebeard.[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/c3e8d544c8bdc0d8dde4d362b8726f4187bc3216.png[/img]

	Versebound is participating in the Myths & Legends Steam sale, so it felt appropriate to enlighten the uninitiated a bit on the mythology our game is based on; [b]Kalevala[/b].

Here's the link to the sale page: https://store.steampowered.com/sale/mythsandlegendssales


[h2]Short history lesson to start off: [/h2]

	Kalevala was compiled in the first half of the 19th century when Finland was developing its national identity. An author called Elias Lönnrot spent years collecting and recording poems from the oral tradition of numerous towns in Karelia and modern eastern Finland. These all he combined into a coherent epic by combining elements, altering details and bridging some gaps with his own writing. 

	The end result is still considered a definitive cornerstone of Finnish national identity and [b]notably influenced elements of Tolkien's construction of the Middle-Earth mythology![/b] I feel the Karelian contribution to this is largely unknown or easily forgotten, hence my insistence we market the setting as "Fenno-Karelian". Anyway!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/a14be0e7ea25534dfa9e10e0dfed73ef99814a66.png[/img]
[i]The Defence of the Sampo (Akseli Gallen-Kallela, 1896)[/i]

	In the world of Kalevala, singing is power. Wounds can be healed, combat won, even life can be created if you're a mighty singer and know the right lyrics to pray with. When the old sage Väinämöinen cuts his knee open with an axe, he desperately goes door to door seeking someone who knows the magic words to sing his wound shut. In exchange, he sings him the origin story of iron. Another time Väinämöinen clashes with the dead giant Vipunen slumbering underground for his long lost lyrics on how to enter the Kalevalan world of the dead, Tuonela safely.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/fd64ca5b2b31f1e50464daef69adb1bd04c89273.jpg[/img]
[i]Kullervos Curse (Akseli Gallen-Kallela, 1899)[/i]

	Knowledge may thus be power, but that doesn't mean the characters are all wise and reasonable. Joukahainen is a cocksure youth whose blustering and envy ends up with a watery end for his sister. Kullervo is the end result of childhood spent in abuse and slavery; an unstoppable ball of anger issues and bloodlust, bringing ruin to his family and only finding peace at the end of his own sword. Even Väinämöinen, the "steadfast old sage" has his blunders; the hubristic horny old man can't take a hint when a young lady says no to marriage until she joins the fish and mermaids. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/02ba51c45a9b0459d26e8cae17f67aa706bc1afc.jpg[/img]
[i]Joukahainen's Revenge (Akseli Gallen-Kallela, 1897)[/i]

	What else? Every animal and plant has a progenitor-mother called Emuu you would pray for help when dealing with their offspring, pains we're caused by a goddess of pain either boiling people's pains in a black pot or milling them on a stone, the firmament (aka dome of heaven) is like a giant pot lid that the legendary blacksmith Ilmarinen crafted to hold up and form the sky of our world... The stories in Kalevala and our folklores are endless.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/80884608085a2079b15f6af9d6ca28bfac7f30b4.jpg[/img]
[i]The Aino Triptych (Akseli Gallen-Kallela, 1891)[/i]

	This game has been a great excuse for me to spend a lot of valuable gamedev time researching these tales and they still keep delighting and sparking my imagination. If even a fraction of that inspiration shines through and leaves you with an appreciation for the setting, I will consider Versebound a textual success!

notes.title: Meet the team!
notes.content:
[h1]Meet the team[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/9e1cfa5969cdd7d6e28dbad3eb5ab0cb9f8bb0ab.jpg[/img]

Hi! Last week we had a team meeting in a burger restaurant! We try to refresh ourselves by having these recreation days from time to time. This time though, the burgers were so big and greasy, that I don't know how refreshing we felt after the meeting. Anyways, here you can meet the core of our team. 

[h2]The core team (founding members of Conifer Digital and the people behind Versebound)[/h2]
On the far left you we can see [b]Pertti.[/b] He's the man behind all of the mechanics and coding in our game. For those who don't know, this is our first game even though some of us have done some smaller game jam projects in the past. Considering this, and the fact that Pertti didn't know almost any coding in the start of this project, it's truly astonishing how fast he has learned. He's also very driven person, and the CEO of our company Conifer Digital Ltd.

Next, in the middle corner with a very handsome beard, we have [b]Jyri[/b]. The second founding member of Conifer Digital. He's responsible for almost all the beautiful in-game graphics in our game, including the maps, character designs and shaders. He's also our lore king! His dedication to studying Kalevala and drawing inspiration from it, writing texts, and building the story around Versebound is very much appreciated. I couldn't imagine anyone better for this job. He has also improved his artistic skill over the course of this game tremendously. Jyri is a very kind person at heart, and he always thinks of others. 

And then, the last but not least: there's me ([b]Joonas[/b]) on the right, holding the camera. I'm the third founding member of Conifer Digital. I'm responsible for the UI, sound effects and also some in-game art. Lately I have also taken the responsibility of doing our marketing. I have a long history of doing music and working with sound, including doing sound effects for a commercial movie. I have also trained my eyes over the years to understand all the intricacies of visual design, so I feel like my job description in this company fits me very well. 

Overall, we have a very motivated and close team. We are good friends with each other and everyone has their job description match their skills. We are excited to launch Versebound this spring for you all.

[h2]Associates[/h2]
Over the course of developing Versebound, we have had a few interns as well as other associates. In the picture above there's Benjamin and Aapo. 

[b]Benjamin[/b] (second from the left with a red hat) is amazing at drawing. With 30+ years of experience doing comics and doing all kinds of graphical work, we are very happy to have him on our team. He has done some beautiful images for us, including the portrait photos of our playable characters in-game, and a new Steam capsule (which we will release soon). He's a very kind person with a lot of interesting stories. We are happy to have him :) Here's a picture he made before the meeting, just for fun:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/6bc02131965486c63c526c952815f3999d7e005d.jpg[/img]

[b]Aapo[/b] (in yellow hoodie and hat) is our newest intern. He's studying game design, and started his internship with us a few weeks ago. So far Aapo has been tweaking all kinds of things in Versebound with great attention to detail. To name a few, there will be new precise statistics of weapon upgrades visible in the level up menu in the next patch, and also a better balance. Aapo has proven himself to be a very valuable asset in our team, helping us all.

[h1]Game updates[/h1]

[h2]Unlocking Tuonela[/h2]
We made a cool quest event for unlocking the second level of our game, Tuonela! It takes place in Tapiola, and required a great sacrifice..

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/4cb4792cf8f72626951d0bd98c1231a82903920b.png[/img]

[h2]Finished the final artifact of our game[/h2]
Finished the final Artifact of our game! It is a classic “Defy Death” item that gives you another chance and can turn around a spicy run!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/473f61981de912c782a4a30f3e10a8b92eb2dbe9.gif[/img]

[h2]Other game updates[/h2]

[list]
[*] Finished the second secret boss of Tuonela! This one is a nasty creeper called Kiputyttö (The Pain Daughter, or something..). So, you can imagine what her company does to you! The attacks are quite simple, but double as deadly! And they look pretty dang good, if you ask me (*patting my own shoulder)
[*] Implemented all of the normal enemies of Tuonela! It is a various bunch of characters brought to life by the skillful hand and mind of our artist, Jyri! There is something for every taste: enemies from tiny to gigantic, some equipped with teeth and fangs, some with your classic iron age weapons and even some with magical skills to throw you off balance!
[*] Introduced our newest trainee to the group: Aapo! The awesome game dev student from Jamk (Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences) started his work with overhauling the text content logic for our Level Up screens and creating SFX’es.
[*] Did a custom event for Tuonela! There is a bridge, and there is crumbling and furious shaking. You can figure out the rest ;)
[*] Made progress with the Task system! Tasks are given by Ilmarinen, the great smith who rewards you with new challenges, working as the backbone of progression in Versebound.
[*] Upgraded a couple of Artifacts to be a bit more impactful (and cool)! The first one is a crow that collects XP for you, but now it also brings Berries once in a while! The second one is a fairy that upgrades nearby XP diamonds for you, but now it also collects them. Handy!
[*] Added a credits panel to our main menu! Now every player can check who amazing people have contributed to the existence of Versebound! 🙂
[*] Level 2 has now been lit, sprinkled with pickups, fogged up and overall gotten to the state where it’s 99.9% ready for its first proper playtests!
[/list]

See you again soon! We have a LOT of new and cool things coming on the course of this spring. Stay tuned!

notes.title: Death has a garden!?
notes.content:
[h1]Happy new year! 🥳[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/12073d2d3c8d7865d1768ba97a7ef1e97c9239c7.jpg[/img]

We've been enjoying the holidays. Sometimes it means enjoying northern lights, sometimes updating new content to Versebound. 

Now the christmas is gone, but the holidays still keep on going. Next up: New year! Next year is gonna be BIG! Versebound will release and [b]change the world forever. [/b]But in the meantime, we wish you happy new year, hopefully everyone got some nice woolen socks for christmas like we do every year. 

Here are some updates we managed to squeeze into the holidays:

[h2]Kuoleman puutarha (Death's Garden)[/h2]
Finished the second Tuonela Ritual! This one is a nod to a famous Finnish painting by Hugo Simberg: Kuoleman Puutarha (Death’s Garden). In this one you’ll have to collect flowers for a nice skeleton who then rewards you with an upgrade to your Skill! I feel that this Ritual works really well and is yet again a new way of taking advantage of the simple mechanics of our game! It was also fun to make some placeholder art for the tutorial, since we had a proper real world reference!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/858c355d8d26be67d681f5946bd338464764e13b.png[/img]

[h2]Tuonela[/h2]
Continued working on Tuonela stuff (the 2nd level of Versebound): This time we implemented a new mechanic to two of the native enemies of the level: as they die, there is a chance that they spawn bullets. So now you, as the player, have to stay alert since bullets can come from anywhere! But don’t worry, it doesn’t always happen! I’m not sure if that’s good or bad though, since you can never know…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/c3ca9a9a23bd634df95155ea6a0689528ee7ed22.gif[/img]

[h2]Other notable progress...[/h2]

[list]
[*] Sprited and placed the second Tuonela Ritual in the map. Always leaves us sad having to replace Pertsa’s beautiful placeholder art.
[*] Finished the sprites for first of Tuonela’s three secret bosses! A hapless player will soon regret releasing these poxes from their prison.
[*] Gave sprites to the last of Tuonela’s level bosses Syöjätär, this ogress will stomp you right to next week.
[*] Sprited our third player character. Way trickier to use, but all the more satisfying to succeed with. Also has a backstory tragic enough to rival Kullervo, but let’s keep her a secret for now…
[*] Added graphics to the dangerous Northern Breeze! It’s something we have to face every day here in Finland…
[/list]

See you next year :)

notes.title: New map!
notes.content:
A warm hello to each and everyone of you who are interested in the development of Versebound! Days are short here in Helsinki, and that cuts the energy to do anything to half (at least for some of us). Even with snow on the ground, it's already dark outside after the first sip of the morning coffee xD Nevertheless, we have made some good progress:

[h1]First secret boss for our second map![/h1]
And estimated the working hours for this task way too low (the estimate was 6h and actual hours almost double).. xD Usually these days we get them quite on point, but I guess that sometimes it’s good to drop the ball big time to remind ourselves of our mortality, especially when it comes to quaternions.. Also there was one really funny bug resulting from Unity thinking floats are ints. It turned our game into a real bullet hell!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/13f06148a95f234f3c7e40a7fdc361d5e607d2c6.gif[/img]

[h1]The second map is now mostly finished![/h1]
It took some playtests, feedback rounds and reworking or scrapping material but I believe the end result plays to our game's strengths while offering a meaningful contrast to our first level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/1fb40574717169646a2277d85b65e00d364b2e22.png[/img]

[h1]Hacked together a shader to make one status effect transition better.[/h1]
Being blinded has never looked this beautiful.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/f1fd0420b7d9f52ccea654a10de417d3c89b4f3a.gif[/img]

[h1]Added new icons & runestones for Poem of Henki![/h1]
Can you guess what it does?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/60b880dcba9ebcbfd3f925a3ab7e3311eca778de.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/e1b3aa14ddcfeab2e0bad57e3d2d24cbe10a0a58.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/6c2a794226f459b12d2304962d04906a9e97edc9.png[/img]

And also the most important part of our progression:
[h1]our placeholder name game is on another level![/h1]
We usually name stuff in our game with some fitting placeholder names whenever the correct name is not known yet. Two of the newest additions have been Markku (a Trial where enemies get a “Mark” on time intervals) and Esko (a classic ESCOrt mission), which are very traditional Finnish names!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/36e4e32d74707e0eff00c82e042a57ff4f0dfe88.png[/img]

[h1]Here's a list of other changes & news:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Added our newest Artifact to the Hub! In our game, whenever you unlock a new Artifact or a Weapon, it will be visible in your Hub in some way. We feel that it is a nice way to make the players feel that they’ve made some progression in the game. Also decorating your home is always nice 🙂
[*] Created second to last Trial for the game! Trials work as difficulty modifiers, creating layers of difficulty into Versebound, while also adding replayability for the players who like to come up with different challenges. When this Trial is active, on time intervals a random enemy gets “Cursed”, becoming more durable and immune to all status effects. After a cooldown, the cursed enemy starts blasting our protagonist with waves of bullets. So you really want to get rid of the Cursed enemies as fast as possible!
[*] While our graphic and lore master Jyri has been working on the second map of the game, Pertti has been busy with creating the content for the map! This time, he created the first Ritual for it. Rituals are timed challenges, which reward the player with an upgrade to their utility Skill. This Ritual is a classic escort mission, where you’ll have to guide a spirit through Tuonela so they can finally find their everlasting peace (Tuonela is all about death, after all). But don’t worry, the spirit cannot be harmed by enemies, so you only have to look after yourself!
[*] Made a modular particle system effect for the environment in our upcoming level 2! It is a thick and evil looking (Jyri will handle this) fog that covers the river that will work as a boundary for the player!
[*] Updated the sprites for the final Trial of Versebound (bye bye placeholder art)! Normally Jyri and Joonas would update the sprites in the editor themselves, but this time the system Pertti had made was so confusing that it took quite a long time even for himself to understand how it works xD
[*] Two more trials have their graphics now! Hope you like being haunted by either the flames of war or a stinky old man.
[*] Workshopped the names and flavor texts for some weapons, some passives, some artifacts, a ritual, a bestiary entry…
[*] Added a new SFX to the weapon Vengeful Tears… Swoosh!
[/list]

Next time we have an update for you will be after the christmas holidays. So marry christmas to all of you! May it be full of happiness and good food :)

notes.title: A sneak peek to the new boss...
notes.content:
It's cold outside and the nights are getting longer. [b]Winter is coming.[/b]

Much like Santa Claus, we come bearing [strike]gifts[/strike] news about Versebound during these long weeks before christmas:

We stumbled upon
[h1]A Spontaneous Dual Versebound Stream![/h1]
It’s been great to see that people are enthusiastic about our game!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/6059536f7354922872bc50d9ba91076476089810.gif[/img]

Pertti, our lead programmer walked in to his dayjob to find that his colleague (who must be tired of hearing him talk about the project) had 
[h1]3D printed some Tonttu's <3[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/ec695cc3c6a45d148ae43b893d18deda26648f62.png[/img]

We got
[h1]One more boss done! [/h1]
This time we created a jumping boss that cannot be harmed during the jump. Fighting this one will require some precise aiming and fancy footwork. It was a really fun process to imitate moving in 3D space even though our game only has two dimensions in use. Also, the placeholder sprite was cute as hell. I’m pretty sure that our artist Jyri will turn it into nightmare fuel though...
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44780665/5f215b5e95b3ce37204f76a9ede9b37e6cfe74b6.gif[/img]

[h2]List of other changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]☠️Tweaked our new boss a bit! Now it actually pushes through any group of enemies to get to you, the protagonist.
[*]🪨In our game, all unlocked content becomes visible in the hub in some way. Added this logic to our newest artifact, which is a nice crow that helps you :)
[*]☠️Continued giving life to the Tuonela bestiary: made a giant boss that smashes ground on time intervals, causing earthquakes and powerful waves that damage and knockback the player. It also sends enemies flying, adding an extra layer of difficulty to this boss. The boss also expands the “Jatuli” race of Versebound, being the second representative of four giant race enemies planned for our game
[*]⚔️New weapon time! Created the first second level -themed weapon, which is a freezing flamethrower that damages and knocks back enemies. The imbued version is a banger too, there is some delicious special behaviour on that one ;)
[*]⚔️New weapon time (again)! Created the starting weapon for our third and final upcoming character. It is a thrust weapon with an interesting gimmick: enemies that are hit with the tip of the weapon always suffer from a critical strike and get a heavy slow for a short duration. This was a fun challenge to tackle, but I think we succeeded well! The programmer art I made for this was even worse than usual, but luckily our great artists will make it look amazing. 🙂
[*]⚔️Created the imbued version of the thrust weapon. It is themed according to the Finnish god of the seas, Ahti. Fitting to the theme, deadly water vortexes are spawned when using this weapon!
[*]🤺Implemented a new trial! Actually the trial was done almost a year ago, last Christmas, but now we finally put it into the system! It is heavily based on the full cursed mode in Enter The Gungeon.. ;)
[*]💎Created a new Artifact! This is one of the coolest ones we’ve made so far for sure! It is a shadow that follows the player but stays behind on utility skill activation, taunting enemies and letting the player reposition themselves. Wow!!!
[*]📖Shortened LV1 intro poem a bit
[*]📖Changed Poem of Haste’s flavor text to a much more fitting one
[*]🖼️Gave that new enemy-pushing boss some swanky sprites and lore based on a karelian god of the turnip
[*]🎵Added new SFX to the Pike Jawbone
[/list]

notes.title: Milestone reached: 100% of poems done (logic-wise)
notes.content:
[h1]Hi! ːsteamhappyː[/h1]
We’re proud to announce that we have reached a small (but big) milestone. The logic (coding part) of poems in our game is the first category to reach 100% completion! It feels super good to say that. 

We have officially started our journey towards the completion of Versebound! This is only the first of many many things that we need to finish, but it’s a big thing for us to have reached this milestone. 

Can’t wait to get this game out and share it with you!

Here’s a list of progress from the last few weeks:

[h2]List of changes[/h2]
[h3]Poems[/h3]
[list]
[*] Created 2 new Poems, which are passive abilities that you collect and level up during each run.
[*] Made some text tweaks for poems
[*] Through these new additions, we now have 100% of the content (logic-wise) of Poems done! This is the first category of content in the project that is done for good. Feels great!
[/list]
[h3]New artifacts[/h3]
[list]
[*] Artifacts are powerful items that players can equip to tweak their playstyle. We discussed new additions with the team and got into an agreement of a few new ones. One of them is a nice crow helper that collects exp diamonds for you :)
[/list]
[h3]First Tuonela boss![/h3]
[list]
[*] Simple but interesting movement pattern: a boss that picks a location based on the player's position and moves towards that until a set duration has passed. Plot twist: the boss is BIG!
[/list]
[h3]Other[/h3]
[list]
[*] UI & Level tweaks
[*] LV2 layout test version out for select few gametesters!
[/list]

More updates are coming soon!

See you in-game,
The Versebound Team

notes.title: Closed Playtest & Next Fest Update!
notes.content:
[h3]Hello from the land of winter (actually it’s still summer here)![/h3]

We’ve been hard at work creating new content for Versebound, and pieces are slowly but surely starting to be where they’re supposed to. Story has been written, lots of amazing art has been created, and we’ve implemented more challenging bosses, new weapons and some completely new mechanics!

Soon, in October to be exact, we are ready to playtest big time again! notes.title: Version Update 240123 / The actually final demo update!
notes.content:
So, the earlier patch (version 240116) was supposed to be the final update for the first demo of Versebound. But, to borrow and make our own version of a classic proverb: [b]Balance.. Balance never changes[/b].

All this of course means that we weren’t happy enough with the balance changes introduced in the last update. The idea was to make the game more accessible for a larger audience, not only for the hardcore gamers. However, we might’ve made the game a bit too easy.

To crack this case, we decided to [b]try out a feature we’ve had in mind for the future updates of Versebound: Trials![/b] Trials are difficulty modifiers that fundamentally change the gameplay, giving players unique challenges that spice up the gaming experience. We feel that this is a great opportunity to test this feature, so all feedback relating to the subject is greatly appreciated!

We also did some tweaks and updates to other stuff as well, you can read about those below.

Now we will (again) declare that this is the actually final version of the first demo of Versebound!
[h3]Happy adventures in the world where verses wield power![/h3]

[b]Detailed patch notes[/b]
[list]
[*] Introduced Trials
[*] Added animations to Tapio’s minions
[*] Tweaked Tapio’s minion spawn specs and minion stats
[*] Reduced damage reduction of Poem of Sturdiness
[*] Reduced healing regeneration of Poem of Recovery
[*] Reduced poem damage bonuses a bit
[*] Reduced Arrows of Ilmatar damage
[*] Reduced Vengeful Tears slow amounts a bit
[*] Tweaked enemy spawn system to make the basic difficulty a bit harder
[*] Small text, visual and other updates
[/list]

notes.title: Version Update 240116 & Future Plans!
notes.content:
[b]For this final patch of our first demo[/b], we went through the feedback we’ve gotten so far, and took the opinions of the amazing people who tried the demo as a starting point for the changes we’d make. We focused on working on what’s already there, since for this demo we didn’t feel that it would be smart to introduce completely new gameplay mechanics. We did make a small exception though, more of that later!

[b]The first main point of this patch is the balance.[/b] Overall, we felt that for most players the game was too difficult. Second, there were some rather great difficulty spikes along the duration of the level, since the power gap of normal weapons and imbued weapons was very big. Third, players felt that the overall balance of poems was quite off, some being much better than others. Same went for the weapons. So, we completely revamped the balance, and almost all weapons and poems went through some changes. Generally the game also became quite a lot easier, the point of this is to make it more accessible for more players. In the future, experienced players will be able to add challenge to the gameplay through various difficulty modifiers, gaining some nice rewards along the way!

[b]The balance update in a nutshell[/b]
[list]
[*] Bridged the gap between normal and imbued weapons: buffed most normal weapons, and nerfed most imbued weapons
[*] Tweaked the spawning specs of the level to make it easier, and also to follow a more linear difficulty curve
[*] To balance the poems, now each poem level also gives %-based boost to all weapon damage. The amount varies, depending on the initial effect of the poem
[*] To underline to importance of poems, we decided to add all 8 runestones to the map, of which player can unlock 6 during a run
[/list]

[b]Second main point of the update is the map.[/b] While we got lots of positive feedback about the atmosphere of the game and the immersive feeling that the map achieves, most players thought that navigating the map was too difficult. Also, there is something hidden in the map that most of the players didn’t uncover. To tackle these things, we
[list]
[*] Added some landmarks to the map, hopefully making it easier to navigate
[*] Added a teaser about something hidden in the map ;)
[/list]

[b]Finally, while players seemed to enjoy the final boss quite a lot[/b], there were also some things that definitely needed improving. Players pointed out that hitting the boss with the weapons was too difficult, and that the fight also needed a bit more of that “horde” element that’s usually present in games like this. So, according to the feedback, we decided to create a new mechanic for the boss fight
[list]
[*] The boss now spawns minions during the fight
[*] Damaging the minions also deal damage to the boss
[/list]

We of course also fixed some bugs, added some quality of life and user experience improvements and as a surprise updated most of the normal enemy sprites with completely new animations!

[b]After this update[/b], we will keep this demo open for about a month to gather some new insights regarding the changes we made. Then we will close the demo and focus on creating some completely new content including new weapons, bosses, characters, progression and brand new mechanics! We will release another demo for the upcoming Steam Next Fest in the summer!

[h3]Thanks for being a part of the journey of Versebound, we hope that you’ll stay tuned![/h3]
